intro: Idaho runs its elections county by county, through each county clerk, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Show a photo ID, such as an Idaho driver's license or ID card, a U.S. passport or federal photo ID, a tribal ID card, or a concealed weapons license. If you do not have one, you can sign a Personal Identification Affidavit instead.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting and in-person absentee voting
dates.detail: Many counties offer early voting, and options vary by county. Early voting ends at 5 pm on Oct. 30.

dates.label: Last day to pre-register to vote
dates.detail: Your county clerk must have your registration by 5 pm local time. After this date you can still register in person at your polling place on Election Day, with a photo ID and proof of residence.

src.label: VoteIdaho.gov — guide to voting in person

dates.label: Absentee ballot application must be received
dates.detail: Your county clerk must have your application by 5 pm local time.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 8 am to 8 pm. A voted absentee ballot must reach your county clerk by 8 pm.
